reasons: The calendar category internship is used by the store but is not in the allowed list.
The persona choices here do not match the database default.
Only 13 of the 24 sections were available, so the remaining definitions from hackathon through settings were not reviewed.

terms.meaning: a version of JavaScript that checks the shape of data before the app runs
a labelled description of what a piece of data must contain
a named type that lists the fields an item must or may have
a list of allowed values, written with vertical bars between them
a field that may be left out, marked with a question mark

sections.name: Priority, EnergyLevel, TaskStatus, TaskBucket
sections.title: Allowed priority, energy and status values
sections.what: Lists the only allowed values for a task's priority, energy level and status, plus the groups tasks can be sorted into.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps labels consistent so every screen speaks the same language.
sections.watch_out: A new status must be added here before the rest of the app can use it.

sections.name: Subtask
sections.title: Subtask item shape
sections.what: Describes a small step inside a task, with an id, a title and whether it is done.
sections.why: Likely reason: a task can be broken into steps the user can tick off.

sections.name: Task
sections.title: Full task item shape
sections.what: Lists every field a task can have, including due date, time estimate, time spent, subtasks, tags, dependencies, recurrence and notes.
sections.why: Likely reason: one complete definition means every screen reads the same fields.
sections.watch_out: Energy level is required here, but tasks loaded from the cloud are not given one, so it may be missing on those tasks.

sections.name: BurndownPoint
sections.title: Burndown chart point shape
sections.what: Describes one point on a project's progress chart: the day, the planned amount left and the actual amount left.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed to draw a burndown chart for each project.

sections.name: Project, HabitFrequency, HabitCategory, HabitDifficulty, HabitStatus, DayCompletionStatus
sections.title: Project and habit choice lists
sections.what: Defines a project's fields and the allowed habit frequencies, categories, difficulties, statuses and daily results.
sections.why: Likely reason: habits appear in several views, so they need matching choices.
sections.watch_out: A new habit category must be added here before the app can use it.

sections.name: Habit
sections.title: Habit item shape
sections.what: Lists every habit field, including name, schedule, streak counts, success and miss rates, skip count, status, day-by-day history, color and icon.
sections.why: Likely reason: one definition keeps habit views and saves in step.
sections.watch_out: The history is keyed by date text, so dates must be written in the same format everywhere.

sections.name: RoutineItem
sections.title: Routine checklist item shape
sections.what: Describes one item in a daily routine: its title, duration, done flag and an optional tip to make it easier.
sections.why: Likely reason: a routine is a checklist, and each item needs its own done status.

sections.name: SystemRoutine, FocusMode
sections.title: Routine shape and focus modes
sections.what: Describes a routine with its checklist, time of day and whether it was done today, and defines the four focus timer modes.
sections.why: Likely reason: one list of timer modes keeps the timer and its settings in agreement.

sections.name: FocusSession, MoodType
sections.title: Focus session and mood shapes
sections.what: Describes a finished focus session, including its tree type, and defines the mood choices for notes.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the tree types, though they give each session a visual.

sections.name: Note
sections.title: Note item shape
sections.what: Describes a note with a title, text, tags, links to other notes, folder, optional mood and timestamps.
sections.why: Likely reason: notes need a consistent shape for saving and display.
sections.watch_out: The folder choices are fixed, so a note saved with any other folder name will fail the check.

sections.name: CalendarEvent, LifeModule, UserPersona
sections.title: Calendar entry shape and life areas
sections.what: Describes a calendar entry and its allowed categories, and defines the life areas and persona choices.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps calendar entries consistent across tasks, assignments and other sources.
sections.watch_out: The category list has no internship entry, yet the store creates internship calendar entries, so the mismatch needs fixing.

sections.name: UserProfile
sections.title: User profile item shape
sections.what: Lists everything stored about the user, including name, level, experience, coins, streaks, freeze tokens, momentum score, weekly history, modules, persona and GPA goal.
sections.why: Likely reason: one profile shape keeps the user's details consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: The cloud profile table lacks several of these fields, such as last active date and weekly history, so cloud saves will not keep them.

sections.name: Course
sections.title: Course item shape
sections.what: Describes a course's code, name, credits, grade, professor and attendance percent.
sections.why: Likely reason: a course needs a consistent shape for the courses view and for the GPA calculations.
sections.watch_out: Attendance is optional here but defaults to 100 in the cloud table, so code reading it must handle an empty value.

sections.name: Assignment, InternshipStatus
sections.title: Course assignments and their deadlines
sections.what: Defines the shape of one assignment: its title, the course it belongs to, its due date, grade weight, and current status (pending, submitted, or graded). The app uses this shape wherever assignments are stored or shown.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Dates such as `dueDate` are plain text, not date objects, so any code that sorts or compares them must parse them first.

sections.name: Internship
sections.title: Internship application record
sections.what: Describes one internship application: the company, role, current stage, when it was applied for, and where the job is. Optional extras such as salary, resume version, and portfolio link can be attached.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: `location` is required while most other details are optional, so new records must always include it.

sections.name: Hackathon
sections.title: Hackathon entry and progress
sections.what: Describes one hackathon the user is tracking, including its dates, the project being built, the team, the tech stack, and a status from upcoming through to won. It also holds an optional progress percentage.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The status values are fixed text choices, so any new status must be added here or the rest of the app may not recognise it.

sections.name: Competition
sections.title: Competition entry and result
sections.what: Describes one competition the user has entered, with its platform, date, status (upcoming, registered, or completed), and optional rank and score once results are known.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: `rank` and `score` are optional, so screens that show results must handle them being empty.

sections.name: ResearchPaper
sections.title: Research paper submission record
sections.what: Describes one research paper the user is working on, with its journal, submission date, publication stage (drafting, under review, accepted, or published), co-authors, and an optional PDF link.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: `coAuthors` is a required list, so records must use an empty list rather than leaving it out when there are no co-authors.

sections.name: Certification
sections.title: Professional certification record
sections.what: Describes one earned certification: its name, the issuing organisation, the issue date, the skills it covers, and an optional link to proof of the credential.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: `skills` is a required list, so it must be present even if empty.

sections.name: Milestone, GoalHorizon
sections.title: Milestones and goal time frames
sections.what: Defines a milestone as a small titled step that is either done or not done. It also defines the fixed list of time frames a goal can use, from daily up to life-long.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The time frame list is a fixed set of text values, so a typo elsewhere in the app will not be caught by the compiler unless the type is used.

sections.name: Goal, BadgeCategory
sections.title: Personal goal and its badge categories
sections.what: Describes one goal: its title, the reason behind it, its time frame, its category, target date, priority, progress percentage, milestones, reward, and linked projects. It also lists the seven badge categories used for achievements.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: `progressPercent` is required here, so any code that creates a goal must set it, usually to zero.

sections.name: Achievement
sections.title: Unlockable achievement record
sections.what: Describes one achievement: its title, description, icon, whether it has been unlocked and when, the experience points it gives, and an optional badge category.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: `icon` is stored as text, so the app must know how to turn that text into a picture or it will show a blank or broken icon.

sections.name: SystemNotification
sections.title: In-app notification record
sections.what: Describes one notification shown inside the app: a title, a message, a timestamp, whether it has been read, and its type (reminder, achievement, deadline, or system).
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: `timestamp` is stored as text, so sorting notifications by time requires parsing it first.

sections.name: SystemSettings
sections.title: App-wide user settings
sections.what: Describes the settings the user can change: theme, sound, notifications, daily focus and task targets, automatic backup, and an optional choice of AI provider between a hosted service and a simple built-in mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: these settings are stored in one place so every screen reads the same values.
sections.watch_out: `aiProviderMode` is optional, so code must decide what to do when it is missing rather than assuming a provider is chosen.

summary: Defines the shapes of the app's data, including tasks, habits, notes, goals and the user profile, and lists the allowed values for each choice.
purpose: Gives every part of the code one agreed description of each data item, so mistakes are caught before the app runs.
why: Likely reason: the app is written in TypeScript, which checks data shapes ahead of time.
how: Lists the allowed choices for priorities, statuses and categories first. Then defines each kind of item as a shape with its named fields. Fields marked with a question mark are optional.
inputs: Nothing at run time. These definitions are read while the code is checked and built.
outputs: No data of its own. The checker uses these definitions to report mismatched fields.
risks: Some values in the store do not match these lists, such as a calendar category named internship that the store uses but this file does not allow. The persona choices here differ from the default saved in the database.
debug: When the build reports a type error, find the field it names in this file, then check the store code that writes that item. A mismatched choice shows up as an error when the code is checked.
